mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in TRANSIT mobility from -10.0 to -27.7 over three weeks signals reduced commuting and discretionary trips, which mechanically lowers weekday and weekend retail footfall and keeps RETAIL_REC below its recent 28-day mean over the next four weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:TRANSIT fell from -10.0 at t-3w to -27.7 at t-1w
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days is higher than over the last 28 days while TRANSIT remains below -20 throughout the forecast window.

mechanism_narrative: When GROCERY_PHARM exceeds 40 percent above baseline, households are stockpiling essentials and diverting trips from retail-and-recreation venues; this keeps RETAIL_REC depressed over the following two weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:GROCERY_PHARM was 48.0 at t-3w and 41.1 at t-0w
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC over the next 14 days rises above its last 28-day mean in periods when GROCERY_PHARM is above 40.0.

mechanism_narrative: The joint depression of WORKPLACES and TRANSIT below -20 reflects a broad shutdown of routine commuting and out-of-home activity; because retail-and-recreation trips depend on these same trip chains, RETAIL_REC stays below its last 28-day mean for four weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:WORKPLACES fell to -40.3 at t-1w and TRANSIT fell to -27.7 at t-1w
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days exceeds its last 28-day mean while both WORKPLACES and TRANSIT remain below -20.

mechanism_narrative: In a stay-at-home policy regime, RESIDENTIAL above 15 percent signals enforced home confinement; retail-and-recreation venues lose discretionary visits and RETAIL_REC remains below its recent 28-day mean over the next two weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:RESIDENTIAL rose from 9.7 at t-3w to 16.9 at t-0w
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC over the next 14 days rises above its last 28-day mean while RESIDENTIAL remains above 15.0.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp week-on-week rebound in WORKPLACES from -40.3 to -21.6 signals that workplaces are reopening and commuting is resuming; this restores weekday retail footfall and lifts RETAIL_REC above its last 28-day mean within two weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:WORKPLACES rose from -40.3 at t-1w to -21.6 at t-0w
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC over the next 14 days remains below its last 28-day mean despite WORKPLACES rising more than 15 points week-on-week.

mechanism_narrative: PARKS mobility is less negative than RETAIL_REC and has stabilized near -20, indicating that outdoor activity is seasonally supported; as outdoor footfall spills into nearby retail-and-recreation areas, RETAIL_REC rises above its recent 28-day mean over four weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS ranged from -19.3 to -21.1 across the four weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days is lower than over the last 28 days while PARKS remains between -19.0 and -22.0.

mechanism_narrative: When TRANSIT falls more than 10 points week-on-week, it signals a new mobility restriction that also cuts retail-and-recreation trips; the negative effect is amplified when WORKPLACES simultaneously drop below -20, keeping RETAIL_REC below its last 28-day mean for one week.

failure_condition: RETAIL_REC over the next 7 days rises above its last 28-day mean following a week-on-week TRANSIT drop greater than 10 points.
